description: Rapid linear peeled transfers along a single chain: funds hop through a short chain of fresh intermediate wallets before reaching the final target.
Swap volatile assets into a stablecoin on the origin chain, then bridge the proceeds to a target chain before final transfer to the destination wallet.
One-to-N splitting: the source fans funds out into multiple parallel intermediate nodes on the same chain, which later converge into an aggregator before the final target.
Layered chain hopping across three distinct chains: funds bridge from chain A to chain B, then immediately bridge again to chain C, where they are finally transferred to the target.
N-to-1 integration: several source streams merge into a single aggregator node, which then transfers the consolidated funds to the final target.
Asset conversion through a decentralized exchange liquidity pool: funds are transferred into a swap node and converted into a different asset before reaching the target.
Deep layered peeling chain: a long sequence of linear hops through intermediate wallets on one chain, maximising the number of hops before reaching the target.
Round-trip bridging: funds leave the origin chain through a bridge, pass through an intermediate chain, and are bridged back to the origin chain before final settlement.
Mixer-style anonymisation: funds are swapped through an asset-conversion node, split into parallel streams, and merged back into an aggregator before the final target.
Repeated same-chain asset conversions: funds are swapped through multiple conversion nodes in sequence to obfuscate the asset trail before the final transfer.
Cross-chain layered integration: two source streams merge on the origin chain and are bridged to the target chain, where they merge again with a local stream before settlement.
Split-then-bridge fan-out: funds are split into parallel streams on the origin chain and each stream is bridged to a different destination chain before re-converging on the final target chain.

Iterative peeling chain: a source or continuation node splits value asymmetrically into a dominant continuation edge and a minor peel edge; the continuation repeats the split and minor peel edges terminate at targets.

Source distributes incoming funds via multiple split edges to a first layer of intermediate nodes, each of which further splits funds to additional intermediate nodes, forming a layered fan-out distribution structure.
Funds from multiple sources merge into a mixer aggregator, then are split into fragmented withdrawals to targets, breaking the link between deposit and withdrawal.
Cross-chain bridge hop to a less-monitored chain, optionally preceded by asset conversion, followed by transfer through a reconstructed destination address.
Multiple victim source accounts merge chaotic irregular inflows into one or few attacker core aggregation wallets, forming consolidation peaks; source accounts are victims and not part of the gang.

Illicit crypto flows fragmented across source branches converge into the attacker's source-chain consolidation wallet, are bridged to a target chain, then transferred into the target-chain OTC/P2P acceptor deposit address for off-chain cash-out.
Multiple source streams on separate origin chains are converted through asset swaps, moved via intermediate transfers, bridged into a consolidation chain, and merged into a single aggregator.
Consolidated funds are fanned out to multiple same-chain OTC/P2P acceptor addresses for off-chain cash-out.
Consolidated funds are swapped into a bridgeable asset, moved via intermediate transfer, bridged to a target chain, and dispersed to multiple OTC/P2P acceptor addresses for final cash-out.
Consolidated funds on the primary chain are split across multiple intermediate addresses, which further disperse to various over-the-counter cash-out points.
An intermediate on the primary chain swaps assets, bridges them to a secondary chain, and then disperses the received funds across multiple over-the-counter cash-out points.
Multiple exploit-origin asset streams on Chain_A are consolidated into an aggregator, then bridged through a peg-out channel to Chain_B and transferred to a destination.

After cross-chain redemption, the held asset on Chain_B is split between a returned portion routed to a restitution sink and a remaining portion that is repeatedly self-transferred along a linear wallet chain.
Illicitly originated assets are consolidated on the origin chain, then bridged to the target chain and received by a destination wallet.
Received funds on the target chain are split between a federation-controlled return wallet and a retained branch that is repeatedly forwarded under attacker control.
Multiple exploit-derived asset streams are consolidated by an aggregator on the origin chain, then bridged to the destination chain and forwarded to a recipient wallet.
Unauthorized assets on the origin chain are spent by an intermediate and split across two cross-chain peg-out outputs into the target chain, each forwarded to a destination for cash-out.
Unauthorized value is created on the origin chain, spent into a cross-chain peg-out, and then split on the destination chain between a returned sink and a retained sink.
A source on the origin chain initiates a cross-chain export that is processed and bridged to the destination chain, where a fabricated import authorization releases drained assets to a target.
Cross-chain entry: a source on the origin chain forwards assets to an intermediate, bridges into the target chain, and consolidates the proceeds into an aggregator.
Outflow obfuscation: aggregated proceeds are swapped through a conversion service into a native asset, transferred onward, and deposited into a mixer sink.
Two attacker-controlled source streams on the origin chain are bridged through a cross-chain service into an intermediate landing point on the target chain.
Landed cross-chain funds on the target chain are split between a privacy-mixer deposit sink and a retained wallet sink.
Victim source funds are drained through multiple malicious approval helper contracts and consolidated into an attacker-controlled aggregator on the same chain.
Attacker aggregator swaps drained stable token balances into native asset and splits the proceeds directly across multiple target addresses on the same chain.
Part of the proceeds is transferred into a privacy mixer while another part is swapped into a stable token and retained in a final wallet.
Cross-chain entry from the origin chain to the destination chain, followed by a transfer and an initial asset conversion.
Funds held in the destination wallet are split into multiple target wallets for dispersal.
Source funds are converted into another asset on the origin chain and bridged to the destination chain.
Bridge proceeds are moved within the destination chain, swapped into another asset, and deposited to a privacy shielding sink.
Borrowed capital and accumulated reward tokens merge into an attack contract, which then converts assets through a vulnerable liquidity pool and extracts proceeds to an attacker-controlled target.
Post-exploit proceeds consolidate briefly and then split between an off-ramp exchange acceptor and a mixer sink for dispersal.

Repeated asset conversion cycles swap exploit proceeds into native asset and merge into a primary accumulation wallet, while a secondary extraction branch routes directly to another accumulation wallet.
Primary accumulation wallet splits proceeds across two holding wallets, while a secondary accumulation wallet transfers funds into a mixing service.
Repeated asset swaps inflate an internal aggregated balance, which is then withdrawn to a target.
Multiple source asset streams are merged into an asset conversion step and swapped into an aggregator internal balance.
Funds on a secondary chain are converted and bridged to the primary chain before a final transfer to a target sink.
External funding and exploited asset proceeds are consolidated through an execution helper into a controlling wallet.
A controlling wallet disperses proceeds across multiple batched transfer branches that converge at an external mixer sink.
External funding and pre-mined token supply converge on a deployer aggregator; the deployer then seeds a liquidity venue and routes liquidity tokens to a burn sink.
A controlling source splits value across several buyer addresses that each swap into the same liquidity venue, fabricating trading volume before the exit.
An attacker-controlled token position is moved through a malicious approval path and swapped through the liquidity venue, with native asset forwarded to a cash-out sink.

Initial funding and token-deployment stage: a funding source splits support to masquerade purchase addresses, which merge into a liquidity pool; the rug-puller extracts proceeds through an intermediate transfer address into a central fund-holding aggregator.

Dispersal from the central fund-holding aggregator: majority is split back to fund a new token launch or liquidity pool, while a minority is routed through an asset-conversion venue into a centralized cash-out acceptor.
Multiple rug-pull proceeds are converted from tokens into native asset, passed through fund-transfer hops, and merged into a central fund-holding aggregator.

A fund-holding aggregator routes proceeds through a shared infrastructure contract that splits them across recipient addresses, which then use decentralized exchange swaps to simulate trading activity.
A fund-holding aggregator splits accumulated proceeds between funding new laundering cycles and cashing out through centralized exchange or swap exit paths.
Multiple exchange hot-wallet funding streams merge into an operational deployer/aggregator, which then forwards funds to a downstream deployment or liquidity-preparation node.

A fund-holding source routes operational funds through a shared splitter contract, which fans out to multiple recipient addresses; one recipient converts assets at a DEX before forwarding to a downstream sink.
A recipient address directly converts assets through a DEX and forwards the converted value onward, simulating organic trading activity while obscuring the funding trail.
Operational funds from multiple exchange hot wallets and a swap conversion consolidate into an aggregator, then pass through an intermediate to the deployment/liquidity target.
Proceeds extracted from the scam liquidity pool pass to an attacker-controlled intermediate and are then split across multiple cash-out target addresses.
Multiple source streams consolidate into a major exchange aggregator on the same abstract chain.
Exploit creates unbacked sidechain asset, then bridges the proceeds to the main chain and transfers them to a destination wallet.
Bridged funds are split on the main chain: a majority portion is returned to the custodian group while the remainder is retained by the attacker.
A source-chain deposit is relayed through an intermediate portal and bridged to multiple destination chains, where cross-chain representations are issued to target-controlled addresses.
